# CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - Bluetooth Allowed Services

Allows only mice, keyboards, headsets, phones via Phone Link and passkeys over Bluetooth, and shuts off file transfer, tethering and serial connections.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Bluetooth CSP ServicesAllowedList (Microsoft Learn, ServicesAllowedList usage guide) and the Bluetooth SIG Assigned Numbers — id and shape verified against DCv2/Settings in pl4nty/intune-change-tracking |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Bluetooth_Allowed_Services.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Bluetooth_Allowed_Services.json) |

> Windows cannot filter Bluetooth by type of device (iPhone, Android, brand), only by service: every UUID on the list is a Bluetooth profile that is allowed, and anything not on it stops working. The list is grouped in blocks, so you can remove or add a block per tenant. BLE basics (1800 Generic Access, 1801 Generic Attribute, 180A Device Information, 180F Battery, 1813 Scan Parameters, 1200 PnP Information) — never remove these; without these six, modern mice and keyboards drop out. Input: 1124 HID and 1812 HID over GATT (mouse, keyboard, pen, game controller). Classic audio: 1108/1112 Headset, 111E/111F Handsfree, 110A/110B/110D A2DP, 110C/110E/110F AVRCP. LE Audio for newer headsets and hearing aids: 1843–1855 (volume, microphone, audio streams, calls, media, Hearing Access). Phone via Phone Link: 111E/111F Handsfree (calls), 112E/112F/1130 PBAP (contacts), 1132/1133/1134 MAP (messages), and Apple ANCS 7905F431-… and AMS 89D3502B-… (notifications and media from an iPhone). Passkeys: FFF9 (phone as passkey via QR code) and FFFD (FIDO security key over Bluetooth). Deliberately not on the list, and therefore blocked: 1105 OBEX Object Push and 1106 OBEX File Transfer (sending files), 1115/1116/1117 PAN (tethering), 1101 Serial Port and 1103 Dial-up Networking. To allow file transfer, add 1105 and 1106 in a tenant-specific copy; to exclude phones, remove the phone block (keep Handsfree for headsets). Windows reads the list when the Bluetooth stack starts: after assigning or changing it, it only takes effect after a restart. Microsoft does not document whether the list also affects BLE advertisements the PC only receives (as with a passkey via QR code); FFF9 is on it to be safe. Sits next to CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - Wireless and Peripherals, no overlap: that one only turns off discoverability, this one decides which services work.
